elements.title: Two-lane rural straight
elements.canon: "Long roads" / "The road consequently becomes a bright ribbon cutting through darker scenery." Compliant by construction; it IS the composition.
elements.data: `highway=primary|secondary|tertiary|unclassified` ways; width from `width=*` when present, else by class (see data-pipeline.md §4); `surface=asphalt` default. Elevation from DGM1.
elements.stone: cross-section construction (crown 2 %, shoulder 1.0 m grass, 0 kerb), edge-line paint geometry.

lane_width_m.note: Eifel B-road 3.25-3.5 m; village 2.75 m. Default chosen for the catalogue: the top of the Eifel B-road band.

asphalt_tint.note: "medium cool grey" here; "Pale roads" for Mediterranean.

texture.look: one repeating 1024 asphalt texture with "subtle normal / very mild roughness variation"; no decals every metre; edge paint baked into the texture strip.

notes: the default road: two lanes, grass shoulder, no kerb. "a narrow two-lane asphalt road".

elements.title: Sweeper (gentle curve)
elements.canon: "Long curves disappear behind hills." The target screenshot is a silver 911 "entering a long sweeping mountain curve". Must be built so the far side is visible or hidden by terrain, never by fog ("Do not hide everything behind thick fog").
elements.data: consecutive OSM nodes with heading change < ~25°/node; radius from three-point circle fit.
elements.stone: superelevation ≤ 4 % on public roads (crossfall banked into the curve; real road practice), centreline smoothing (Catmull-Rom through nodes with G1 continuity).

stone_parameters.centreline_smoothing: Catmull-Rom through nodes with G1 continuity

texture.look: the sweep is one strip mesh; the beauty is the sightline, not the tessellation.

notes: a curve the car takes at speed; the classic "long sweeping mountain curve". Varies: nothing visual.

elements.title: Hairpin
elements.canon: "Mountain roads" / "Much more vertical." Compliant; a hairpin is a silhouette event.
elements.data: node heading change ≥ 120° over < 60 m of way; `highway=*` unchanged.
elements.stone: inner-radius widening (real roads widen the inside by ~1 m), crossfall 6 % max.

outside_barrier.note: a low stone wall (F2) or guardrail (F1) on the outside is the region's call. Default chosen for the catalogue.

texture.look: the inside verge is a single grass/rock texture; no rubber marks, no debris.

notes: a bend > 120°, radius < 30 m (Eifel: Steilstrecke, the road up to Nürburg, alpine passes).

elements.title: Junction (T, Y, cross)
elements.canon: "Intersections" (Autobahn family) and "Roads descend toward villages." Compliant when simple; a junction is 2-4 road strips blended into one flat patch, "recognizable reality represented economically".
elements.data: an OSM node shared by ≥ 3 way ends (or a way passing through). Priority from `highway=*` class ranking; `highway=stop|give_way` nodes for the sign (F6).
elements.stone: patch construction (fillet radius 6-12 m by class), give-way triangle paint.

village_kerb.note: whether a village junction gets a kerb. Default chosen for the catalogue: R15's stone has the kerb.

texture.look: one patch mesh, one blended texture; no traffic islands unless OSM has them.

notes: two or more ways meeting at a shared node.

elements.title: Roundabout
elements.canon: "modest European architecture" applies to infrastructure too: a grass island, a kerb ring.
elements.data: `junction=roundabout` on the circular way; arms are R4 entries onto it.
elements.stone: ring construction (inner island radius = OSM geometry; truck apron 1.5 m).

island_dressing.note: Default chosen for the catalogue: the canon's grass island.

texture.look: island is one disc mesh with a grass texture; no sculpture, no flower beds.

notes: a circular junction (11 in the Ring bbox, live count 2026-09-23).

elements.title: Grade (level) crossing
elements.canon: "Industrial roads pass underneath structures" — rail is scenery, not gameplay. Compliant as a texture event plus two barrier props.
elements.data: `railway=level_crossing` node; the `railway=rail` way for the track strip.
elements.stone: crossing plate 4 m long; barrier post pair.

texture.look: the rails are a 512 texture strip; no animated barriers in 4B.

notes: a railway crossing the road on the level. Zero in the Ring bbox (live count 2026-09-23), so library-defined here and instantiated when a region has one.

elements.title: Crest
elements.canon: "Long curves disappear behind hills." The crest is the canon's main sightline device.
elements.data: not an OSM tag: detected from the draped DGM1 profile (second derivative of elevation along the centreline over 20-40 m windows; see data-pipeline.md §5).
elements.stone: vertical-curve construction from the DEM (no artificial ramps); the profile is never "smoothed away" beyond the 1 m grid's own noise floor.

texture.look: the mesh follows the DEM at 1-2 m spacing along the road only; terrain beyond uses the coarse lattice (T-family).

notes: a convex vertical curve the car can lighten or lift over (Flugplatz, Schwedenkreuz, Pflanzgarten's Sprunghügel). Varies: nothing.

elements.title: Dip / compression
elements.canon: same as R7. The physics dependency (compression loads) is in the car already (car.gd's springs read `sample_height`, see implementation-plan.md gravity section).
notes: a concave vertical curve (Fuchsröhre's bottom, Breidscheid bridge approach). Stone / Varies: as R7.

elements.title: Banked section (the Karussell)
elements.canon: unusual but real: "recognizable reality". Concrete slab seams are in the texture, not the mesh; the *bank* is in the mesh because the car feels it.
elements.data: OSM way 414785755 `name=Karussell surface=asphalt;concrete` (live, 2026-09-23). Elevation: DGM1 is terrain-only and the bank may be smoothed at 1 m; DOM1/DOMB (surface models, same OpenData catalogue) or a manual bank profile: decided in ring-region-decisions.md §3.
elements.stone: banked cross-section construction (parametric: bank angle, bowl width, flat strip).

bank_pct.note: the library says banked ~30 %; the range is chosen for the catalogue. From data or the region table.

bowl_width_m.note: named by the library without a number; range and default chosen for the catalogue. From data or the region table.

flat_strip_m.note: "a thin asphalt strip at the bottom"; the surface-class table's asphalt inner 1 m. Range chosen for the catalogue.

texture.look: the slab pattern is a photographic 1024 concrete texture with slab lines; no per-slab geometry.

notes: a concrete bowl banked ~30 %, "Concrete slabs (steep bank) with a thin asphalt strip at the bottom" (docs/nordschleife-data-sources.md §2). Varies: only the parameters, from data or the region table.

elements.title: Bridge
elements.canon: "Coastal roads expose the sea. Industrial roads pass underneath structures." A bridge is a silhouette landmark; parapets are furniture (F11).
elements.data: `bridge=yes` + `layer=*` on the way; the deck follows the road profile, not the DEM (DGM1 shows the valley under it: the deck's elevation is interpolated from the abutments).
elements.stone: deck construction (slab + parapet, span from OSM geometry).

parapet_style.note: stone in villages, steel on B-roads, concrete on Autobahn. Default chosen for the catalogue: the B-road's.

texture.look: a box deck and two parapet strips; piers are plain cylinders or slabs.

notes: road over a river, road or valley (188 `bridge=yes` highway ways in the bbox; Breidscheid's is the Ring's lowest point at ~320 m).

elements.title: Tunnel
elements.canon: "A tunnel needs a convincing entrance silhouette but doesn't require individually modeled concrete imperfections." Portal is what matters; inside is a dark tube with lamp pools.
elements.data: `tunnel=yes` + `layer=-1` on the way; the terrain is NOT cut: the portal (F12) is stamped on the DEM surface and the road passes under the T-mesh.

lamp_spacing_m.note: named by the library without a number; range and default chosen for the catalogue.

texture.look: interior is one tiling 512 concrete texture + emissive lamp quads; "small pools of illumination".

notes: road through a hill (28 `tunnel=yes` highway ways in the bbox; "Tunnels cut directly into mountains" in the Alps family).
Varies also: the sound profile (deferred; user-thoughts-economy.org line 93).

elements.title: Embankment cut
elements.canon: "Road embankments." and "Grey rock faces." The cut face is a silhouette and a texture.
elements.data: derived: where the DGM1 cross-slope at the road exceeds ~15 %, the assembler builds a cut/fill profile so the road platform is flat across (the DEM already contains the real cut; the element gives the face its material and its edge).
elements.stone: platform-flattening rule (road always level across, ± crossfall).

face_material.note: Default chosen for the catalogue: the canon's "Grey rock faces".

texture.look: the face is the terrain mesh with a rock texture; no boulders.

notes: the road cut into a slope: uphill cut face one side, downhill fill the other.

elements.title: Motorway / dual carriageway
elements.canon: Autobahn family, "wet grey infrastructure contrasted with the glossy car". Not in the Ring bbox (no `highway=motorway` there; A61 is east of it); library-defined, first instantiated when focus reaches an Autobahn region.
elements.data: `highway=motorway|trunk` with `oneway=yes` pairs; `lanes=*`; central reservation from the gap between the two carriageways.
elements.stone: carriageway construction (hard shoulder 2.5 m, central barrier F13).

lanes.note: per carriageway, from `lanes=*`; range and default chosen for the catalogue.

wet_weather_variant.note: S6 is deferred past the Ring.

texture.look: concrete texture with expansion joints baked in; big gantry signs as textured quads.

notes: "Wide road. Concrete. Guardrails. Large road signs."

elements.title: Slip road / link
elements.data: `highway=motorway_link|trunk_link|primary_link|secondary_link` (B 258 has 9 primary_link ways in the bbox).

texture.look: a strip with a painted taper; the merge nose is one triangle patch.

notes: on/off ramps and junction links. Varies: nothing visual.

elements.title: Village street
elements.canon: "Roads descend toward villages." "Small villages." Compliant: the village is where the road slows and the B-family stands by it.

parked_cars_per_100m.note: 0-3 per 100 m; canon says "few". Default chosen for the catalogue.

texture.look: kerb is part of the road strip's cross-section (no separate mesh); cobbles are texture.

notes: the road inside a settlement: narrower, kerbed, houses close ("A village can simply contain: 8 houses, church, stone wall, few parked cars, trees, road signs").

elements.title: Track / gravel access
elements.canon: "Large stretches where there simply isn't much there." Drivable but plain.

surface_texture.note: Default chosen for the catalogue: the surface-class table's road_gravel_512.

texture.look: one 512 gravel texture; ruts are in the texture, not the mesh. Physics: a surface friction class per `surface=*` (deferred to the world-profile work; see implementation-plan.md).

notes: farm and forest tracks; the Ring's gravel service roads (5 gravel raceway ways in the bbox).

elements.title: Circuit segment (the Nordschleife itself)
elements.canon: the Ring is the proving ground ("Though nurburgring is where we test the cars") and it is a *road*, not "an artificial racing arena": guardrails and trees, no grandstand clutter except where OSM has grandstands (B4).
elements.data: OSM relation 38566 `type=route route=road name="Nürburgring Nordschleife"`, 52 member ways `highway=raceway oneway=yes` (live pull 2026-09-23: 20 746 m summed, 1 119 nodes, mean node spacing 19.4 m; official 20.830 km).
elements.stone: the centreline source (relation 38566 pinned to its snapshot), the kerb paint pattern (red/white 0.5 m kerbs on the inside of bends only), the F1 guardrail run on both sides where OSM has no `barrier=*` saying otherwise.

texture.look: kerbs are a texture strip; guardrails are F1 instances at 4 m posts; no sponsor boards.

notes: a raceway way: one-way, kerbs painted, guardrail-lined, 8-9 m wide (docs/nordschleife-data-sources.md §4; note OSM carries `width=5` on 22 of its 52 ways: an open question, recorded in ring-region-decisions.md).
Varies: nothing: the Ring is put in stone.

elements.title: Pit lane / access link
elements.canon: this is where the proving-ground office (E11) stands; a link, not a landmark.

barrier_type_at_gate.note: the library names the barrier arm prop only.

texture.look: a barrier arm prop and a booth; "toll infrastructure" in the canon's words.

notes: the Döttinger Höhe entrance and exit to the public Nordschleife ("Anbindung zur Nordschleife", way 26543901, 16 nodes; T13 pit lane ways).
